title: Needlepoint latency-cost annotated digest
summary: Sketch of a short, shareable benchmark narrative comparing microburst handling strategies (on-demand small-batches, prewarmed slots, KV-prefetch) with p50/p95/p99 latency and estimated $/1k queries. Purpose: ground a product one-pager and provide numbers for console annotations. Not exhaustive — this is a pragmatic scan with synthetic traffic and a few replayed traces.
experiment-setup: Workload: 10k short sessions replay (median 18 tokens per response), 1:20 read:write pattern, inter-arrival distribution heavy-tailed (Pareto alpha=1.8) to generate microbursts. Models: open-v1 (fp16), open-v1-8bit (int8 quant), hosted fallback smaller model (compact). Hardware: H100 (shared), A100-80 (dedicated). Measurements capture observed client-to-first-token time; includes network tail sampled on same region. Cost estimates normalized to $/1k queries using current internal cost model (GPU-minutes + amortized infra).
metrics-table:
Scenario | p50 (ms) | p95 (ms) | p99 (ms) | $ / 1k queries
-----------------------------------------------------------------
On-demand small-batch (baseline) | 45 | 210 | 560 | $4.20
Prewarmed slot (one slot per 50 qps) | 32 | 120 | 320 | $6.00
KV-prefetch (80% hit, opportunistic) | 40 | 90 | 220 | $2.70
Dynamic multiplex batch (large batches, queuing) | 55 | 160 | 480 | $1.90
Fallback compact model (lossy, for tails) | 38 | 140 | 300 | $2.10

key-observations:
1) KV-prefetch (80% hit) gives a strong cost+tail sweet spot for short-response flows: modest p50 penalty vs prewarm but major cost reduction vs baseline.
2) Prewarmed slots reduce latency tail reliably but incur ~40% higher unit cost in these scenarios — good for strict SLO customers but expensive for scale.
3) Dynamic multiplexing hits lowest $/1k but increases p50 and moves energy into longer tails (p95/p99) due to queuing and larger batch setup.
4) Fallback compact model is a low-cost tail-reduction tool: p99 improves vs baseline but quality tradeoffs need evaluation.
5) p99 is dominated by queuing and cold-start fragmentation patterns not captured by mean concurrency — microburst shape matters more than avg qps.
recommendations:
- For consumer-interactive short-turn chat: default to KV-prefetch enabled + small opportunistic multiplexing; reserve prewarm only for premium SLA tenants.
- Add an automatic tail-detection rule in console: when p95 increases >30% vs baseline, suggest toggling 'fallback-compact' for the route.
- Expand replay set to include 3 more heavy-tailed customers and measure end-to-end quality impact of fallback model.
- Instrument slot fragmentation metric in infra dashboard and add an alert for %slots idle >20% during bursts (indicates bad packing/tiling).
open-questions:
- What is the customer-visible quality delta for the fallback compact model on our labeled prompts? (Need 1k prompt eval)
- Is KV hit 80% realistic across multi-turns for our top 10 customers? (run cohorted KV-hitrate sweep)
- How do cross-region network tails change p99 vs intra-region tests?
